Neotraditonal or New American traditional. They hold, have varied line weights, and tend to mix in a lot of surrealistic imagery which really appeals to me. It's very versatile while still flat enough to not create too much spacial illusion, so it can flow with the body without distracting from the natural curves and slopes of the body. I'm not a fan of horror, gore, or biomechanical type tattoos. The first two are kind of tacky, and the final one distracts from the natural beauty of the way a body flows, I think. I also don't like portrait tattoos, just because your body already has a perfectly good face and the idea of having a realistic image of anyone else's face on your body is unsettling. Those are just my opinions, though. To each their own.

Water color and geometric tattoos looks lovely. It's a shame that water color tattoos probably fade more rapidly than other pieces. White ink and henna style tattoos are beautiful too but they fade super fast. White ink looks great at first but then it either fades to the point of near invisibility, scars because the artists went too deep by mistake, or it turns a weird brownish yellow as it tans more rapidly than the skin around it. Shame.

Black light tattoos seem like they need to be studied more before I'll believe they don't cause cancer.

New school tattoos and super old school American traditional tattoos are okay, I guess. They don't really appeals to me. New school messes with space and creates dimensional illusions and American Traditional lacks the pallete and level of detail that come with more elaborate styles. It feels very limiting.
